newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's parliament starts 1997-98 budget debate.
newsitem.headline: Iran's parliament starts 1997-98 budget debate.

text.p: Iran's parliament on Sunday began debating President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani's proposed budget for the next Iranian year which starts on March 21, the official Iran News daily newspaper reported.

The 188 trillion rial ($108 billion at the official exchange rate of 1,750 rial per dollar) general budget is the Islamic state's biggest ever and will be the last steered by Rafsanjani who is expected to step down after two four-year terms in office after presidential elections later this year.

Tehran, as the world's third largest oil exporter, has been enjoying windfall profits because of international petroleum prices reaching their highest level in recent months since the 1990-91 crisis over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
Iran's oil revenue in the first nine months of the current Iranian year has been more than $14.6 billion, $2.6 billion more than budgeted for, according to officials.

"We expect the deputies will pay particular attention to the problems that are hampering efforts aimed at increasing the export volume of non-oil goods," Iran News quoted an unnamed economist as saying.

Exports of non-oil commodities, such as carpets, have been hit after the government was forced to reintroduce fixed exchange rates and strict controls on the transfer of hard currency after a near free-fall in the rial's value in 1995.
Parliament's open session debate on the budget is expected to continue for several weeks, the paper said.

Rafsanjani submitted the proposed balanced budget -- based on government revenue excluding earnings from state industries and banks of 74.9 trillion rials ($42.8 billion), led by some $17.5 billion of oil export earnings -- to the parliament's Budget Commission in November.
